findings.title: Data race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed in parallel init workers
findings.body: Inside the group.Go closures, `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` are variables captured from the enclosing scope and written by several goroutines at once. Now that BuildIndex no longer holds a global lock, builds really do run concurrently, so these writes race. The result can be a wrong indexed count and corrupted error state. Use goroutine-local variables (`_, _, err := ...`) and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Concurrent builds of the same key and file index collisions
findings.body: The cache lock is now taken only for the final map write. Two callers that both miss in getOrCreateIndex (for example, watch events or searches arriving during startup) will build the same key at the same time. For file-based indexes, both call bleve.New on the same directory, which can fail or corrupt the index. One built index also overwrites the other, and IndexTenants and IndexedKinds metrics get double-counted. Add per-key singleflight or re-check the cache under the lock.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache map without lock
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without holding cacheMu. Other goroutines can write to the map concurrently via BuildIndex. A concurrent map read and write can make the Go runtime throw a fatal error.

findings.title: Search init now runs before the watcher, so events between index build and watch start are lost
findings.body: Init now builds every index synchronously in the constructor. WatchWriteEvents is subscribed only after the indexes are built and starts from the latest RV at that moment. Any writes made while the indexes were being built are therefore never applied to the index. Init also now blocks NewResourceServer startup for the whole index build, with no timeout.

findings.title: Integration test disabled for postgres
findings.body: This PR skips the storage server integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure. The new startup-init behaviour therefore goes untested on postgres.
